summary.intent: Port xscreensaver hacks (Blaster, Substrate) to an ESP32 screensaver firmware, resolve review findings on each trail/PR, finish and merge the port-hack skill, and capture lessons in AGENTS.md and tickets.
summary.outcome: Blaster (#22), Substrate (#24) and the port-hack skill (#19) were merged to main, with a Blaster NULL-deref fix and a stronger drawing test. AGENTS.md was revised and pushed straight to main. Issues #23, #25 and #26 were filed, and memory and journal entries were written.

repo: Hack sources (e.g. blaster.c, substrate.c) must stay byte-identical to upstream. Fixes go in wrapper files such as blaster_safe.c or substrate_single.c, which include the original with XSCREENSAVER_MODULE emptied and re-register the hack.

blaster_free loops NUM_ROBOTS over robots[], but robots is only allocated on the first draw. Freeing before the first draw is a NULL deref (exit 139 in the dump tool at 0 frames). The generic test test_every_hack_can_be_stopped_before_its_first_frame covers it.
A single-precision wrapper took Substrate from about 121 ms to about 38 ms per step. It needs M_PI as a float literal, and literals like 0.81 stay double.
Display push cost rose from 31 ms to 41-45 ms (issue #23). Compare device numbers against a same-build baseline.
The runner now paints each hack's background (white for Substrate), so tests that assume a black start can be vacuous. The draws-something test now compares against the canvas as the hack started.

Ports in flight conflict in registry.c, test_hacks.c, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, platformio.ini exclusion lists, and tools/assessment_measured.md. The generated assessment is regenerated by the scorer, not hand-merged.
Pinned builds still rotate after 90 s, so use -DROTATE_SECONDS=0. A Substrate restart takes about 27 minutes, so estimate restart time from cycles x frame time.
Two plain 868 KB mallocs reach PSRAM on the device.
The git info/exclude file is shared across worktrees. Local main is checked out in the main checkout, so it can't be fast-forwarded with git fetch origin main:main. Use git merge --ff-only there.
Finding about sandGrains division by zero was a false positive: sandg is a float, so inf/NaN does not trap, and trans_point bounds-checks.

code.finding: test_every_hack_can_be_stopped_before_its_first_frame lives here, registered at line 245. It was the mutation check that caught the Blaster crash.
The runner clears to the hack's background colour instead of black. This made the older starts-black and draws-something tests vacuous for Substrate.

workflow: Mutation checks and red-first stub hacks reveal tests that pass for the wrong reason.
Verify delegated agents' reports yourself. They were wrong about a test count and about byte order.
After a fresh git fetch, confirm a merge by checking the branch tip is an ancestor of origin/main. A stale local ref gave a silent false negative.
Force-pushing a branch may reset the Entire trail approval. Use --force-with-lease, and ask the user first for published branches.
Findings made before a rebase can become stale when they reference code that has since landed. Verify the claims against the tree before dismissing them.
AGENTS.md carries rules and gotchas, and the skill carries procedure and recipes. AGENTS.md revisions go straight to main, with no PR.

friction: The first force push of the Substrate branch was rejected by GitHub transiently and needed a retry.
Rebasing Substrate onto main after Blaster merged took five conflicts across the six commits, mostly in shared registry and measurement files.
git branch -d refused because local main was stale, so -D was used after an ancestor check. Local main could not be fast-forwarded with git fetch because it was checked out.
The Substrate restart estimate was wrong: about 3 minutes against an actual 27.
A blanket edit added a double free to a test. The suite crashed immediately and caught it.
The shell's working directory was firmware/, so the commit path was doubled once.
Entire's approvals gate showed 'no reviewers approved' after a force push, even though the user had approved.
open_items: Issue #23: the 41-45 ms display push regression, with the setSwapBytes A/B test not yet done.
Issue #25: dry-run test of the port-hack skill's 'choose which hack to port next' step.
Issue #26: review README.md (it says thirteen hacks, with stale fps and push numbers) and add a pointer to the skill.
The board is still running a Pyro-pinned, rotation-off build and needs a normal flash of current main.
Substrate's rebased branch was never re-flashed on the device.
SKILL.md is about 680 words, over the 500-word guidance.
The user plans to optimise AGENTS.md later (about 2,980 words). The approvals-gate note records a single observation.
Issue #6 (dirty-rect idea) could help with the push cost.
